title: latency-spike-diff-debrief
content:
Context:
- Investigating sporadic 60-300ms outbound latency spikes observed in the streaming path over the last 36 hours (prod, region-us-east-1). Spike correlates with bursts of small requests (avg tokens 8-12) hitting the continuous batching multiplexer.
- PR under review: runtime PR #4827 (streaming backpressure adjustments). Suspected root causes: batching backpressure threshold logic + lock contention in request queue draining.

Quick summary of what I saw locally:
- Reproduced a micro-burst with k6 (scripts/stream-burst-k6.js) using 200 concurrent connections sending small prompts. Observed tail latencies on server process.
- perf map (perf record + flamegraph) indicated hot path in runtime/streaming/multiplexer.cpp -> tryDrainBatch() holding queue_mutex for >5ms during peaks.
- Threads waiting on queue_mutex show stack frames that include createResponseFuture() and writeToWire().

Immediate review notes for PR #4827:
- Good: author added an exponential backoff for batch formation and split the fast-path vs slow-path loops.
- Risky change: moved the write-to-wire call inside the queue-locked section for a retry path. That appears to reintroduce blocking IO while holding mutex.
- Missing: no new unit tests for lock-free fast-path; no integration test that simulates heavy small-request burst.
- Telemetry gaps: no histogram of queue-hold-time or per-request lock-hold-time. We need metrics before/after to validate.

Checklist (code review) — things to validate before approving:
1) Locking: ensure writeToWire() is called outside queue_mutex scope except when a truly necessary state mutation requires it.
   - Files to inspect: runtime/streaming/multiplexer.cpp, runtime/streaming/request_queue.h
2) Batching heuristics: confirm early-exit thresholds do not starve tiny requests in presence of many in-flight large requests.
   - Validate batchSizeTarget and maxWaitMs semantics in tests.
3) Non-blocking IO: any path that may block must either use async IO or be scheduled on an io-thread pool.
4) Observability: add two histograms: streaming.queue_lock_ms and streaming.batch_formation_ms; wire to cloud metrics.
5) Safety: fallback policy when queue depth > critical threshold should route to cheaper model variant (per routing policy) instead of blocking.
6) Regression tests: add k6 scenario to CI that runs the burst script in a short post-merge smoke.

Proposed minimal patch to unblock and keep risk low:
- Revert the write-to-wire relocation in tryDrainBatch() so writes happen after queue unlock.
- Add a small wrapper to record lock hold time in microseconds (RAII timer: QueueLockGuard + metrics.inc).
- Make backoff change opt-in via runtime flag (experimental.streaming.backpressure_v2) to allow canary.

Suggested canary rollout plan (for Dedicated/Hosted):
- Stage: feature flag off by default for 1% of traffic on cluster-us-east-1a for 24h.
- Telemetry: stream new histograms to infra-metrics with 1m cardinality tag (canary=true/false).
- Guardrails: if streaming.queue_lock_ms P95 increases > 20% or error_rate > 0.1% in canary, auto rollback.

Suggested tests to add (quick list):
- unit: batch heuristics boundaries (zero tokens, max tokens, mid-range).
- integration: k6 stream-burst hitting a real binary with a mock model that returns immediately (to isolate multiplexing).
- e2e: load test with real-model small-token bursts for 1 minute, assert P95 latency not worse than baseline + 5%.

Notes-to-self / follow-ups (action items):
- [ ] Add QueueLockGuard timer and wire to telemetry – small PR, target: runtime telemetry sprint. (owner: me)
- [ ] Patch to ensure writes happen outside the lock; add comment explaining invariants (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Create k6 CI job using scripts/stream-burst-k6.js; add to lightweight nightly smoke (owner: Noelle)
- [ ] Add feature flag for backpressure_v2 and a canary-handling hook in routing layer (owner: platform-eng)
- [ ] Open ENG-1193 ticket to track long-term: consider refactor to lock-free SPSC queue for multiplexer.

Unresolved questions / things to ask the author:
- Why was writeToWire moved inside the locked section? Author note says to avoid ABA in state machine, but need to see a short repro and comment.
- Are there any downstream contract assumptions that expect synchronous write semantics (client connectors)?
- Is the new backoff heuristic intended to reduce cost or latency? The code comments are ambiguous.

Small refactor idea (low-effort, high-signal):
- Introduce MultiplexerDrainToken struct that captures snapshot of batch contents while holding lock, then unlock and invoke drain using the token. This isolates state mutation and avoids holding mutex during IO.
- Replace the current two-mode branching with a small state-machine in request_queue.h with clear docs and invariants.

CLI snippets used for repro (notes):
- k6 run scripts/stream-burst-k6.js --vus 200 --duration 1m --out influxdb=http://local-influx:8086/db
- perf: perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof inference-runtime) -- sleep 30; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

Mental model summary (short):
- The system is sensitive to tiny-request microbursts. Holding a global queue mutex while performing any IO amplifies tail latency. Fix is to minimize critical sections and add observability so regressions show up as histograms, not just SLO spikes.

Notes-to-self (quick log):
- 2025-02-10 09:38 PST: pushed QueueLockGuard timer prototype to local branch calvin/lock-timer, still needs tests.
- 2025-02-10 11:02 PST: brief sync with Maya — she will open the small revert PR and annotate where invariant was violated.
